chapter_title: The Chapter of the Name of the Fathers
chapter_note: Short, highly substrate chapter presenting a three-fold emanation hierarchy mapping divine beings to their cosmic dwelling-places. The teaching structure is: being → realm of greatness → established in it. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system (no contemporary application, no institutional content, no exhortation). Dialogue frame is confined to opening paragraphs. The seam flag on ¶4 is a false positive — institutional vocabulary field is empty. Negative editorial fatigue (-6.00) confirms substrate increases toward chapter end. Compare chs. 7 and 25 for the same emanation hierarchy pattern.

paragraphs.core_text: The Father of Greatness, as he is named; due to what reason is he given the name 'the Father of Greatness'?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula 'Once again the enlightener speaks to his disciples:' — standard hagiographic attribution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive cosmological question defining the teaching topic: the correspondence between the name 'Father of Greatness' and the cosmic reality it designates. The question itself structures what the teaching will map. Persian pedagogical tradition.

Heavy formulaic disciple response (dialogue_frame score 37.93). 'We beseech you, our master, that you may enlighten us' is pure honorific frame. The question 'who is it that is named the Father of Greatness?' echoes ¶1 without adding new cosmological content.

paragraphs.core_text: The Father, who is the first established thing, shall be called 'the Father of Greatness'. His greatness is the great earth where he lives, he being established in it [...] the essence of the light that swathes all the rich gods and the angels and the dwellings [...] is set over it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution 'Then he speaks to his disciples:' and transitional 'Now,' which connects the editorial frame to the teaching answer.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core substrate teaching: maps the Father to his cosmic dwelling (the great earth / land of light). The formula 'his greatness is X where he lives, he being established in it' is the structural template that ¶4 and ¶5 iterate. Lacunae suggest manuscript damage. 'The first established thing' is cosmogonic priority language — the Father as ontological ground.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, they shall call the Third Ambassador 'father'. His greatness is the light ship of living fire wherein he lives, he being established in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second iteration of the being→realm mapping. The seam flag is a FALSE POSITIVE: institutional vocabulary field is empty. Both sides of the mapping are cosmic: Third Ambassador → light ship of living fire (= sun). 'Furthermore' is a list continuation marker within the enumeration, not an editorial bridge connective. The mapping structure is identical to ¶3 and ¶5.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, Jesus the Splendour shall himself also be called 'father'. His greatness is the ship of living waters where he lives, he being established in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third and final iteration of the being→realm mapping: Jesus the Splendour → ship of living waters (= moon). 'Once again' here functions as list continuation (parallel to 'Furthermore' in ¶4), NOT as dialogue frame formula. The three-fold structure (Father/great earth, Ambassador/ship of fire, Jesus/ship of waters) maps the emanation hierarchy to cosmic dwelling-places. Complete teaching sequence.
